I farm only 5 mu, so I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all of it. With some family labor working off-farm, I will choose a management style that is steady and not too risky: reliable seed, moderate fertilizer, fewer but timely field operations, and full use of my well irrigation. For wheat, I will use an improved variety because I want stable yield and good stand establishment through the winter-spring season. I will till with rotary tillage because it fits my scale and is easier to manage than deep ploughing every year. I will apply nitrogen as the main nutrient, with phosphorus to support roots and some potassium to keep the crop stronger. I will irrigate a few key times because water matters a lot for wheat in my area. For maize, I will plant a hybrid because I want higher yield on limited land. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize, keep the same 5 mu in production, and stay with rotary tillage for convenience and speed. I will use a bit more nitrogen on maize than wheat, keep phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels, and irrigate when the crop most needs it. I will not overdo pesticide sprays, but I will still make enough applications to protect yield if pests, disease, or weeds become a problem. My goal is stable output from both crops rather than chasing the highest possible yield with high cost.
